explain.title: Angles in standard position
explain.body: The angle is said to be in standard position if: (a) Its vertex is located at the origin of the coordinate plane. (b) One of its rays (the initial side) lies along the positive x-axis. The other ray is the terminal side.

explain.title: Positive, negative, and co-terminal angles
explain.body: A positive angle turns counterclockwise from its initial side; a negative angle turns clockwise. Co-terminal angles have the same initial and terminal sides and differ by a multiple of 360° or 2π rad.

explain.title: Degree and DMS measures
explain.body: A degree is 1/360th of a full rotation. Also, 1° = 60′ and 1′ = 60″. To change decimal degrees to DMS, multiply the decimal part by 60 for minutes, then multiply any leftover decimal part by 60 for seconds.

explain.title: Radian measure and conversions
explain.body: A radian is a unit of angular measure in mathematics, particularly in trigonometry. It is defined as, “the angle subtended at the centre of a circle by an arc whose length is equal to the radius of the circle”. A full circle is 2π radians = 360°. Use 1° = π/180 rad and 1 rad = 180°/π.

explain.title: Arc length and sector area
explain.body: When θ is in radians, arc length is ℓ = rθ and area of sector is A = 1/2 r²θ. If the angle is given in degrees, convert it to radians before using these formulas.

mistakes: Using 360° when a formula needs the full circle in radians, 2π.
Using π/180 to convert radians to degrees instead of 180/π.
Forgetting to multiply the decimal part of the minutes by 60 to get seconds.
Using the sector formulas with an angle still in degrees.
Confusing clockwise and counterclockwise rotation, or giving only the quadrant and not the co-terminal angle.
Leaving off units: lengths use cm and areas use cm².

explain.title: Name the sides from the chosen angle
explain.body: The side opposite the right angle is the hypotenuse. From the chosen acute angle, the side across from it is the perpendicular, and the side beside it (not the hypotenuse) is the base.

explain.title: Use the textbook's definitions
explain.body:
For this right angled triangle ACB, the trigonometric ratios of an angle “θ” are defined as:

sin θ = Perpendicular/Hypotenuse = a/c : cosec θ = Hypotenuse/Perpendicular = c/a
cos θ = Base/Hypotenuse = b/c : sec θ = Hypotenuse/Base = c/b
tan θ = Perpendicular/Base = a/b : cot θ = Base/Perpendicular = b/a

explain.title: Remember the reciprocal ratios
explain.body:
NOTE:

(i) cosec θ = 1/sin θ

(ii) sec θ = 1/cos θ

(iii) cot θ = 1/tan θ

explain.title: Relate tangent to sine and cosine
explain.body: The textbook shows that tan θ = (a/c)/(b/c), so tan θ = sin θ/cos θ. Similarly, cot θ = cos θ/sin θ.

explain.title: Use complementary angles
explain.body: The textbook states: sin(90° − θ) = cos θ; cos(90° − θ) = sin θ; tan(90° − θ) = cot θ; cot(90° − θ) = tan θ; sec(90° − θ) = cosec θ; cosec(90° − θ) = sec θ.

Using the hypotenuse as the base or perpendicular; the hypotenuse is always opposite the right angle.
Reversing a ratio, for example writing sin θ as hypotenuse/perpendicular instead of perpendicular/hypotenuse.
Forgetting that sec, cosec and cot are reciprocal ratios.
Mixing up complementary identities, such as writing sin(90° − θ) = sin θ instead of cos θ.
In a verification question, stating the result without showing the ratios and multiplication.

explain.title: The three fundamental identities
explain.body: The Pythagoras theorem says: “The square of the length of the hypotenuse of a right triangle is equal to the sum of the squares of the lengths of the other two sides”. Dividing a² + b² = c² by c², b² and a² gives sin² θ + cos² θ = 1, tan² θ + 1 = sec² θ, and 1 + cot² θ = cosec² θ. These are called Pythagoras identities.

explain.title: Finding ratios from one given ratio
explain.body: Make a right triangle using the given ratio, then find its missing side using the Pythagoras theorem. Since θ lies in the first quadrant, the side lengths and the trigonometric ratios are positive. Use the side definitions to find the ratios and their reciprocals.

explain.title: Proving an identity
explain.body: An identity proof uses equal expressions to change one side into the other. Start with L.H.S or R.H.S, show each algebraic step, and use the trigonometric identities or ratio definitions where needed. Stop when the expression matches the other side.

mistakes: Confusing the side positions: sin θ = perpendicular/hypotenuse, cos θ = base/hypotenuse, and tan θ = perpendicular/base.
Forgetting to take the positive square root for a side when θ lies in the first quadrant.
Changing both sides of an identity at once without showing that the expressions remain equal.
Using sin² θ + cos² θ = 1 incorrectly; for example, replacing sin² θ by 1 − cos² θ is valid, but replacing it by 1 − cos θ is not.
Forgetting to square both terms when expanding a squared expression, or losing the middle term in a binomial expansion.

explain.title: The 45° triangle
explain.body: In the textbook's square, each side is 1 and the diagonal is √2. The trigonometric ratios are: sin 45° = a/c = 1/√2 ; cosec 45° = c/a = √2; cos 45° = b/c = 1/√2 ; sec 45° = c/b = √2; tan 45° = a/b = 1 ; cot 45° = b/a = 1.

explain.title: The 30° and 60° triangle
explain.body: The perpendicular bisector of an equilateral triangle with side 2 makes a right triangle with sides 1, √3 and 2. The textbook gives: sin 30° = 1/2 ; cosec 30° = 2; cos 30° = √3/2 ; sec 30° = 2/√3; tan 30° = 1/√3 ; cot 30° = √3. For 60°: sin 60° = √3/2 ; cos 60° = 1/2 ; tan 60° = √3; cosec 60° = 2/√3 ; sec 60° = 2 ; cot 60° = 1/√3.

explain.title: Read the special-angle table
explain.body: These results in the form of a table can be written as: θ: 0°, 30° = π/6, 45° = π/4, 60° = π/3, 90° = π/2. sin θ: 0, 1/2, 1/√2, √3/2, 1. cos θ: 1, √3/2, 1/√2, 1/2, 0. tan θ: 0, 1/√3, 1, √3, ∞.

explain.title: Convert degrees and radians
explain.body: Use 180° = π radians. To change degrees to radians, multiply by π/180°. To change radians to degrees, multiply by 180°/π. For example, 255° = 255π/180 = 17π/12 radians.

explain.title: Use reciprocal ratios and identities
explain.body: The reciprocal ratios are cosec θ = 1/sin θ, sec θ = 1/cos θ and cot θ = 1/tan θ. Useful identities include sin² θ + cos² θ = 1 and sec² θ − tan² θ = 1.

explain.body: Work on one side at a time. Replace tan, cot, sec or cosec with expressions in sine and cosine, use known identities, and simplify until that side matches the other side.
